about: Receiving waters for Michigan MiEnviro CSO/SSO reports (source mi-egle-mienviro-cso-sso-list) that name a permit and outfall but sit on no water page: rows of the untraced-outfall worklist of 2026-11-28 (4,590 reports with a permit and outfall and no water) whose key starts with MI|. One entry per permit, or per permit and outfall group where outfalls go to different waters. Research only; nothing applied. Distances are from the stated point to each record's own outline (openboatlaunch out/water/<slug>.json or the record's inline NHD geometry), measured with build.status.water_geometry and shapely on 2026-11-28.
decisions: MI0022802 outfall 082 (246 reports): placed on river-rouge-detroit-mi (the lower-Rouge remainder) by the Oakwood facility's location and outfall 109's ECHO point; the resolver's remainder rule would send a pointless 'Rouge River' to river-rouge-mi, so this needs an explicit placement (or outfall 109's point lent to 082 as its successor, which would be our inference and should be labelled).
MI0022802 outfall 104 (1 report): the report names the Rouge River but the Conner Creek basin is on the Detroit River 15 km away; placing on detroit-river-mi overrides the report's text.
MI0043982 outfall 001 (105 reports): St. Louis Creek has no NHD or GNIS name found; build a hand record from the creek's NHD flowline, or decide whether to start the reach on trap-rock-river-mi.

Duplicate river records found while choosing: paint-river-mi and paint-river-mastodon-mi overlap at Crystal Falls; st-joseph-river-mi and saint-joseph-river-jonesville-mi overlap at Niles and Jonesville. The remainder records were built against a different parent (paint-river-iron-river-mi, saint-joseph-river-mi) than the openboatlaunch record that already covers the stretch.

The worklist notes still list river-rouge-detroit-mi, saint-clair-river-algonac-mi and paint-river-mastodon-mi as candidates although each is a covers_part_of remainder of another candidate; merge_remainders should have set them aside when no point is given. Check that path runs for name matches with no point (status.py around the 'names N waters' note).
Aliases the reports need: 'Raisin River South Branch', 'River Rasin', 'St. Joe River', 'Big Cedar River', 'Beguns Creek'/'BeGunns Creek'.

entries.why: Port Huron WWTP, St. Clair County. Of the two 'Saint Clair River' records, saint-clair-river-mi (openboatlaunch, GNIS 1624885, bbox lat 42.619 to 43.003) runs from Lake Huron at Port Huron down to Marine City; saint-clair-river-algonac-mi is the NHD remainder of it (covers_part_of saint-clair-river-mi, bbox lat 42.526 to 42.619, Clay Township near Algonac), about 35 km downstream of Port Huron. The plant's ECHO outfall 001 (42.977456, -82.418548) is 262 m from saint-clair-river-mi and 40.8 km from the Algonac record. All of Port Huron's St. Clair River frontage lies on saint-clair-river-mi. The reports name the St. Clair River (not the Black River, which also receives Port Huron CSOs; outfall 005 is on black-river-port-huron-mi), so the river they name is the main record at Port Huron. The resolver's own remainder rule (merge_remainders: with no point, a remainder steps aside for its main record) gives the same answer.

entries.why: Dearborn CSO. These two outfalls name the main Rouge River (the same permit's other reports say 'Rouge River, Lower Branch' when they mean the Lower Rouge). The candidates: river-rouge-mi (openboatlaunch, bbox -83.311 to -83.144, the main Rouge from Oakland County down through Dearborn) and river-rouge-detroit-mi, which is the NHD remainder of it (covers_part_of river-rouge-mi): a stretch from about -83.143, 42.291 down to the mouth at Zug Island in Detroit and River Rouge, plus a 20 m stub at 42.632 in Oakland County. The permit's registry outfalls on the main Rouge in Dearborn (009, 013, 014, 016, 017, 117; ECHO points) were all tied to river-rouge-mi; outfall 014 is 19 m from it and 5.3 km from the remainder. Dearborn's reach of the main Rouge lies upstream of the remainder. 011 and 015 have no point in ECHO, so a position downstream of the Ford Rouge turning basin (outfall 017's area, 1.1 km from river-rouge-mi and 2.1 km from the remainder) cannot be excluded from a document; the city's reach makes river-rouge-mi the record.

entries.why: GLWA (formerly DWSD) outfall 082 was the untreated CSO at the Oakwood Pump Station (reports: 'Oakwood Pump Station - Sander & Liddesdale', 2001 to 2012). The permit's long-term control program replaced it with the Oakwood RTB and new pump station (outfall 109, in service 2012); the 2019 permit no longer lists 082. The Oakwood facility is on Pleasant St between Deacon and Liddesdale in southwest Detroit, and its discharge reaches the Rouge River 'using the O'Brien Drain', which runs north from the facility. O'Brien Drain has no water record; it is a short enclosed drain, so the reach starts in the Rouge. ECHO's point for outfall 109 (42.2836, -83.1419), the same facility and drain, is 324 m from river-rouge-detroit-mi and 1,111 m from river-rouge-mi; the permit's outfall 056 'Fort St. (Oakwood District)' at 42°17'27" N 083°08'33" W is 7 m from river-rouge-detroit-mi and 328 m from river-rouge-mi. The Oakwood district's Rouge frontage is the lower Rouge below Fort St, which is the river-rouge-detroit-mi remainder. Note: the resolver's remainder rule would send a pointless 'Rouge River' to river-rouge-mi; this outfall needs the explicit record (or outfall 109's point) instead.

entries.why: Conner Creek CSO RTB, on Detroit's east side at the mouth of Conner Creek (ECHO point 42.3628328, -82.958461), 15 km from the Rouge. The permit says 'Outfall 104 discharges to Conner Creek'; Conner Creek is enclosed and has no NHD or OSM record (registry no_water_reason), and the basin discharges at its outlet on the Detroit River. 21 of the 22 MiEnviro reports for this outfall name the Detroit River; the one in the worklist names the Rouge River, which is a slip in that report. The water it really enters is the Detroit River. Decision: placing it on detroit-river-mi overrides the report's own text, so the page should say the report named the Rouge River.

entries.why: North Houghton County Water & Sewer Authority CSO (Calumet and Laurium area), outfall 001 'the intersection of First Street and Isle Royal'. EPA's permit list gives the receiving waters 'St. Louis Creek; Douglas Creek'. No record of that name exists in data/waters-*.json, and the registry's NHD builder found no NHD flowline or waterbody of that name in Michigan (nearest named NHD stream: Scales Creek). A Keweenaw waterfall guide describes St. Louis Creek as a small creek from swamps near Laurium in the Trap Rock River system, with St. Louis Falls at 47.22895, -88.40872, about 1.6 km southeast of the ECHO outfall point. So the creek runs to the Trap Rock River (trap-rock-river-mi exists) and on to Torch Lake (torch-lake-hubbell-mi). Not found in GNIS from here; it may be an unnamed NHD flowline locally called St. Louis Creek. Build a hand record for St. Louis Creek from the outfall point down to the Trap Rock River from the NHD flowline it follows; until then the reach can start at trap-rock-river-mi only if the owner accepts the downstream water as the entry water (it is not what the report names).
